what: Paycom sells payroll and HR software to American companies, and unusually it makes employees enter their own payroll data through its Beti product, which cuts the errors employers pay to fix.
customers: Mid-sized American employers, on monthly fees per employee.
money: payroll, HR, time and talent modules billed per employee per month
setup fees and interest on client payroll funds
moat: Payroll is changed reluctantly: a conversion risks paying people wrong, which no HR director wants to own. Retention runs around 90% year after year.
risks: Revenue growth has slowed from the 25%-plus of earlier years
Beti reduces the services revenue Paycom used to earn from fixing payroll errors
Interest on client funds is a meaningful profit source and falls with interest rates
opportunities: A 22.1% net margin and $659M of free cash flow on $2.2B of revenue
23 times earnings for a business with recurring revenue and 90% retention; analysts see about 13% upside
watch: Recurring revenue growth and the annual retention rate.
